transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Sarah O'Neil (CISO), Tom Baker (Head of Platform), Priya Singh (Compliance)

Summary (auto-generated): Discussed data residency requirements for Maple City Bank, options across Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private, logging and audit constraints for regulated banking data, and next steps to run a technical POC for VPC and logging behaviors.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we want to respect your time, I'm Lena, joined by Raj from our SE team. Could we do quick intros?
[00:12] Sarah (CISO): Sure, I'm Sarah O'Neil, CISO at Maple City. We're evaluating options for hosting LLM inference and have strict data residency and logging requirements.
[00:18] Tom (Platform): Tom Baker, head of platform. We're particularly interested in latency and cost tradeoffs but compliance is the gating factor.
[00:24] Priya (Compliance): Priya Singh, compliance. We'll need to understand encryption, audit logs, and how long request/response logs are retained.
[00:31] Lena: Great, thanks. High level, Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). Today we'll focus on where customer data can reside, how logs are handled, and what controls we can provide.
[00:45] Raj (SE): Quick note, hosted is fastest to get started but by default logs and telemetry might be retained for service health unless you opt into stricter retention; Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and more control, and Private gives you the control plane in your VPC or on-prem.
[01:10] Sarah: For us GDPR applies — we have EU customers and cross-border is a blocker. Also HIPAA applies to certain product lines, so PHI can't leave our approved regions and logs that contain PHI need to be handled differently.
[01:32] Priya: We also need SSO/SAML and RBAC integrated with our IdP, plus audit trails for who accessed model outputs and prompt logs. Retention policy is 7 years for certain records but we may need redaction.
[01:51] Lena: Understood. On SOC 2, we have attestation and a compliance pack we can share. For GDPR, we support region-pin and can run inference in eu-west-1, or you can go Private and keep everything inside your VPC. For HIPAA, we have controls and can sign BAAs for Dedicated and Private deployments — hosted may require extra contractual steps.
[02:20] Tom: Can you clarify Hosted vs Dedicated regarding logging? If we go hosted but region-lock to EU, do logs still go to a central store in US?
[02:33] Raj: Good question. With hosted region pinning, primary compute and data residency are in the region, but some operational telemetry may cross boundaries for service reliability unless you opt for dedicated or private. We can route logs to your SIEM via secure delivery or disable long-term request logs for hosted.
[02:57] Sarah: We need explicit guarantees. Our security team won't approve any telemetry leaving the EU for certain product data.
[03:06] Raj: For that, Dedicated or Private is recommended. Dedicated gives you reservation of capacity in chosen regions; Private, either VPC or on-prem, gives you control of the control plane. In Private we can ensure logging endpoints are your own S3/Blob within the region or forwarded to your SIEM with no copies retained externally.
[03:29] Lena: Also, KMS integration — we support customer-managed keys so you control envelope keys; HSM integrations are possible for Private installs.
[03:40] Priya: For HIPAA, do you have a BAA template? Also, how do you handle PHI in prompt/response logs — is there automatic redaction?
[03:52] Lena: We do provide a BAA for Dedicated/Private. For automatic redaction, we have options: you can disable request/response logging entirely, strip PII client-side before sending, or we can run post-processing redaction rules. There's no perfect auto-redaction for all edge cases, so we usually recommend a combination: data classification client-side + redaction + short retention.
[04:18] Tom: About network — can we do VPC peering or private link? We have strict egress rules.
[04:26] Raj: Yes. For Dedicated we support private networking and peering, and Private supports VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and on-prem connectors. We'll share the VPC networking guide.
[04:37] Sarah: What about audit logs for who invoked particular prompts and which user saw outputs? We need immutable audit trails.
[04:45] Raj: We can integrate with your audit logging pipeline and push structured logs to your S3 or SIEM; logs can include request metadata and identity but we can omit full prompt text if needed or store only hashes. Retention policies can be enforced on your side for immutability and archival.
[05:12] Lena: Quick aside — many customers worry about KV cache stuff and token caching leaks. We have isolation for KV caches per session and can opt out of certain caching features for regulated workloads.
[05:30] Tom: What's the performance hit if we disable KV caching?
[05:33] Raj: There is measurable latency and cost impact depending on workload. For short sessions it's minor, for long rolling chat histories it can be significant. We can run benchmarks in your environment to quantify.
[05:50] Priya: On GDPR, we need data deletion proof — can you delete all logs and provide attestation?
[05:58] Lena: Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can execute deletions and provide audit evidence. For hosted, we have deletion APIs and we can provide logs showing deletion, but customers often prefer Dedicated/Private for stronger contractual guarantees.
[06:15] Sarah: Any third-party subprocessors? We need list for DPIA.
[06:22] Lena: We'll provide the subprocessors and a data processing addendum.
[06:28] Raj: One detail — model variants: we can route to smaller quantized models for cost, but for PHI workloads you might want vetted model variants with strict determinism; we can recommend Redwood-verified profiles.
[06:47] Tom: How are credentials handled for service-to-service? Do you support short-lived tokens and fine-grained scopes?
[06:54] Raj: Yes, we support short-lived tokens, scoped API keys, and integration with your secret manager and KMS.
[07:06] Priya: For logging retention, if we need to cap request logs to 30 days, but keep audit hashes for 7 years, is that possible?
[07:15] Raj: Yes — you can configure separate retention for full-text logs vs metadata/hashes. We'll document the retention policies and the mechanism.
[07:28] Lena: Can I ask about your timeline and stakeholders?
[07:32] Sarah: We're aiming to decide by end of August. Stakeholders include security, platform, legal/compliance, and procurement. We want a POC this month if possible.
[07:44] Lena: Good — we can run a short POC. The POC typically validates regional routing, VPC peering, and logging retention behavior. Raj can lead the technical run.
[07:55] Raj: Proposed POC steps: 1) network setup (VPC peering/PrivateLink), 2) run sample workloads, 3) verify logs are routed and retention rules apply, 4) run a small privacy audit and deletion exercise.
[08:13] Tom: Sounds good. What about pricing? If we go Dedicated reserved capacity, is that a long-term commit?
[08:20] Lena: Dedicated is typically reserved monthly/annual with commit levels. We can provide pricing ranges and sizing guidance after the POC and after reviewing expected token volumes. Hosted is pay-as-you-go but may not meet your residency constraints.
[08:33] Sarah: One more thing — legal wants to know about e-discovery and subpoenas: if we need logs for legal holds, can Redwood preserve them?
[08:42] Raj: If logs are stored in your account (Private), you control legal holds. For Dedicated, we can set retention and preservation policies per contract; for hosted, we'd need to coordinate.
[08:55] Priya: Regarding encryption at rest — we require CMEK (customer managed encryption keys).
[09:01] Lena: Supported for Dedicated and Private. We'll surface key rotation and KMS policies in the artifacts we share.
[09:12] Sarah: Do you have HIPAA customers in financial services or other regulated industries? Any references?
[09:19] Lena: We have customers in healthcare and finance and can provide redacted reference briefs and compliance contacts under NDA.
[09:27] Raj: Technical note — if you need on-prem, our on-prem package can run air-gapped with local control plane; that's the maximal control option.
[09:39] Tom: For that on-prem path, what's the operational burden on our side?
[09:43] Raj: It requires some ops work — provisioning GPUs, networking, and an install window. We provide install automation and a support engagement for the first few months.
[09:56] Lena: I'll call out a few common objections we hear: 1) hosted easier but not always acceptable for compliance, 2) dedicated lowers cross-tenant risk but has cost/commit constraints, 3) private/on-prem gives max control but increases ops overhead.
[10:12] Sarah: That matches our internal discussion. We probably want to evaluate Dedicated and Private, run POC, then choose.
[10:20] Lena: Great. Raj, any specific data points you want to capture for the POC?
[10:24] Raj: We'll need sample request volumes, representative prompt shapes, example size of chat histories, and which logs must be retained vs redacted. Also the network contact for peering.
[10:36] Tom: I'll send an inventory doc with token estimates and sample prompts.
[10:40] Priya: I'll send the compliance checklist and which data fields are PHI.
[10:45] Sarah: We'll also need pricing scenarios for quarterly vs annual reserved Dedicated capacity.
[10:51] Lena: Noted — we'll include that in the follow-up.
[11:00] Raj: Quick technical caveat — there may be small transcription mismatches if we parse logs for compliance, so we recommend using structured logging with hashes and metadata to reduce exposure.
[11:15] Tom: Understood. Any issues with certs or mutual TLS for private links?
[11:20] Raj: We support mTLS for PrivateLink and peering endpoints. We'll include cert rotation guidance.
[11:29] Priya: On retention proof, what form does your deletion attestations take?
[11:34] Lena: Typically a deletion log with timestamps and identifiers, plus a short attestation statement signed by our security team. For Dedicated/Private we can offer deeper contractual language.
[11:48] Sarah: Okay let's recap next steps.
[11:52] Lena: Recap: we'll send SOC2 and HIPAA artifacts, Raj will send VPC guide and POC plan, customer to send sample prompts and compliance checklist, we'll schedule a 1-hr POC kickoff next week.
[12:08] Tom: One last micro question — are you able to run inference on quantized LLMs with same audit controls?
[12:15] Raj: Yes, we support quantized model variants; auditing/logging are orthogonal and can be applied equally. We'll point to the model profiles.
[12:27] Sarah: Thanks everyone.
[12:29] Lena: Thanks — we'll follow up with artifacts.
[12:33] End of call.
